P.strength: Home AR phone: the one-line edition bar, compact heading and intro bring the 11.9% figure with its universe (adults 15+, Findex 2021) into the very first screen, the fastest route to an answer of the five.
P.weakness: Sources /data/ AR phone: the table of contents is a cramped two-column grid of small underlined links, tiny targets that look like an English sidebar squeezed onto a phone.

Q.strength: Sources /data/ AR phone and Record CLM-001 AR phone: the boxed numbered contents and the large section numerals make each section and the way to the source easy to spot and tap.
Q.weakness: Home AR phone: the edition bar wraps to two lines and large bordered 'cite / report an error' buttons sit above the introduction, so a first-time reader scrolls past controls and a topics list before any figure appears.

R.strength: Record CLM-001 AR phone: generous body size and leading with the green section numeral and double rule give a clear, recognisable record structure.
R.weakness: Record CLM-001 AR phone and Home AR phone: the Latin serif 'Global Findex 2021' inside a bold Arabic sans title and the heavy bold lead paragraph read as an English design mirrored into Arabic rather than set in it.

S.strength: Sources /data/ AR phone: a single-column numbered list separated by thin rules, underlined links and one button style make the whole system feel calm and consistent with very few element types.
S.weakness: Record CLM-001 AR phone: the section heading '01 ما الذي يثبته هذا الدليل؟' is set in small grey text, so the sections, including what the evidence does not establish, are hard to find while scanning.

T.strength: Payments domain AR phone and Record CLM-001 AR phone: the largest, best-leaded Arabic body text and clearly sized numbered section headings make a one-minute read and the search for the boundary comfortable on a 390 px screen.
T.weakness: Record CLM-001 AR phone and Payments domain AR phone: a two-line edition bar, a kicker and four-line titles (with the Latin serif line) push the first sentence of the answer far down the first screen.

P.strength: Home EN desktop and Record CLM-001 AR phone put the claim, its scope (adults 15+, surveyed areas), the 23%-not-surveyed limit, the 2.8-point margin and the measurement clock all inside the first screen, and Payments AR phone reaches the 'what it does not establish' block before the first scroll.
P.weakness: Home EN desktop and Record EN desktop leave the right half of a 1440 viewport empty with no sidebar, so the route to the evidence-record list and the section index is weaker than the others, and the Arabic phone views are set tight enough to feel cramped.

Q.strength: The numbered right-hand index on Record EN desktop lists '04 What this evidence does not establish' and '05 Original source and verification' at a glance, and the large body size on Record CLM-001 AR phone reads comfortably.
Q.weakness: Home AR phone places boxed 'Cite this page / Report an error' buttons above the introduction at the same visual weight as the primary actions, and the oversized green '01' plus the misaligned bulleted topics grid on Home EN desktop add UI energy and special cases without serving the reader.

R.strength: The serif display, double gold rule and quiet sidebar on Home EN desktop and Record EN desktop give the register of a serious journal while the evidence record list and 'Original source and verification' entry stay in view.
R.weakness: On Record CLM-001 AR phone the Latin 'Global Findex 2021' inside the Arabic title inherits the English serif, and on Home AR phone the large bold lede outweighs its own section heading, both signs of a composition mirrored from English rather than designed in Arabic.

S.strength: Home EN desktop's two-column hero gets the 11.9% figure with its scope into the first screen while keeping the sidebar's evidence-record list and section index, and Sources AR phone's single-column numbered index is the cleanest route to the original-source material of the five.
S.weakness: On Home AR phone and Record CLM-001 AR phone the cite and report links sit between the title and the content, and the medium-weight body on Record EN desktop makes the long paragraphs slightly heavier than they need to be.

T.strength: Record EN desktop and Record CLM-001 AR phone keep the measurement clock and population directly under the title, separated from the body by a double rule, so provenance is read before the figure.
T.weakness: The four-line serif title on Record EN desktop and the display headline plus cite/report links on Home EN desktop push the first evidence figure to the very bottom of the first screen, and the serif Latin inside the Arabic title on Record CLM-001 AR phone shows the heading face was not set for Arabic.

P.strength: Most information per first screen: the Payments AR phone view shows the question, the figure paragraph, the CTAs and the 'what it does not establish' section all before any scroll, and the Home EN desktop puts the 11.9% figure with its clock block in view.
P.weakness: The Home and Record EN desktop views leave the right third of a 1440 screen empty with no section navigation or record list, and the Record EN desktop meta labels carry a stray '?:' double punctuation; the Sources AR phone TOC is crammed into two columns that are hard to scan.

Q.strength: Numbered section navigation (01-09 on Home EN desktop, 01-06 on Record EN desktop) and the 'Evidence records behind these figures' sidebar make the route to the boundary section and the underlying records the most scannable of the five.
Q.weakness: Boxed 'Cite this page / Report an error' buttons sit above the lede on every page (Home AR phone, Record AR phone, Home EN desktop), and the bulleted four-column Topics list and the card-style numbered TOC on the Sources AR phone add chrome that pushes the first figure off the phone first screen and makes the register busier than a statistical office.

R.strength: The serif display headings with the gold double rule (Home EN desktop, Record EN desktop) give a recognisable journal-like identity while keeping the sans body measure comfortable.
R.weakness: In the Record AR phone view the Latin 'Global Findex 2021' fragment is set in a serif inside a bold Arabic sans heading, which reads as mirrored English rather than designed Arabic; the Record EN desktop also repeats the '?:' meta-label bug, and the boundary section is not visible on the Payments AR phone first screen.

S.strength: The cleanest and most consistent page grammar: clock and universe labels are correct and adjacent to the title on Record EN desktop and Record AR phone, cite/report are quiet text links on every page, the Sources AR phone TOC is a single ruled column, and the two-column hero on Home EN desktop uses the width without a decorative sidebar.

T.strength: The most formal register: serif title, cite/report links tucked under the title, a gold rule separating provenance meta from body on Record EN desktop, and clean 'When was it measured' labels, which is the closest of the five to a serious statistical journal.
T.weakness: The Home AR phone first screen is spent on an eyebrow, the title, cite links, the lede, two CTAs and a heavy bold Arabic statement, so no figure appears before scrolling, and the Record AR phone heading mixes serif Latin with bold Arabic sans in the same title.
